generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the work you are already doing. Almost every assignment you take on asks you to be critical: an essay that must weigh evidence, a report that judges a method, a seminar where views are tested rather than simply repeated. The students who treat being critical as a habit, and run it on purpose, are the ones whose work improves from one assignment to the next rather than repeating uncritical moves. Treat what follows as being about your own essays, reports and reading, not about study in the abstract.

The same habit runs through professional practice. Wherever you must weigh evidence, question a claim, or decide something with reasons, being critical is what separates a sound decision from an assumption. The ability to question, weigh and judge is one you keep long after you graduate.
